Table 12: Townships in each class, sfdep’s pooled null against the period-conditional null, for all five variables. Only classes that occur in either are shown.五个变量在 sfdep 混合零模型与按期条件化零模型下各类别的镇区数。只列出在任一方案中出现的类别。





Consequence. For all conflict events, sfdep classifies 40 townships as oscillating hot spots; the period-conditional null leaves 2. Most of the others become sporadic or consecutive hot spots, which is what the heat strip in Fig. 7 suggests they are: townships that have been violent relative to the rest of the country for most of the period, not townships that were once unusually calm. The persistent cold spots fall from 32 to 5, because quiet townships in the quiet early quarters are no longer counted as significant. The same shift appears in all five variables.


后果。 就全部冲突事件而言,sfdep 把 40 个镇区归为振荡热点;按期条件化的零模型只剩 2 个。其余大多变为零星或连续热点,而这正是 Fig. 7 中的热力条带所提示的:它们是在 研究期大部分时间里相对于全国其他地区一直暴力的镇区,而不是曾经异常平静的镇区。持续 冷点从 32 个降到 5 个,因为平静早期季度中的平静镇区 不再被算作显著。同样的变化出现在全部五个变量中。



7.3.3 Defect 3: a class rule that ignores the sign缺陷三:一条忽略符号的分类规则

sfdep tests a township against its class rules in a fixed order and assigns the first that fits. Its rule for an intensifying hot spot asks for significance in at least 90% of quarters, including the last, and a significant upward trend, but it counts significant quarters of either sign and never checks that they are hot. It is also tested before the rule for a diminishing cold spot. A township that is a significant cold spot almost throughout, and whose Gi* is rising towards zero, is therefore called an intensifying hot spot. The cold version of the rule already counts only cold quarters, so the hot version is corrected to match (ehsa_rules() in R/ehsa.R), and nothing else in the rule set is changed.


sfdep 按固定顺序用各条分类规则检验一个镇区,并赋予第一个符合的类别。它对增强热点 的规则要求包括最后一个季度在内至少 90% 的季度显著,且有显著的上升趋势;但它统计的是 任一符号的显著季度,从不检查这些季度是否为热。而且这条规则排在减弱冷点 规则之前。因此,一个几乎始终是显著冷点、且 Gi* 正向零回升的镇区,会被称为增强热点。 冷点版本的规则本来就只统计冷季度,所以本研究把热点版本修正为与之一致(R/ehsa.R 中的 ehsa_rules()),规则集的其余部分不作任何改动。



Code
EH$rule_fix |>
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(ts_an)[, c("TS_PCODE", "TS", "ST")], by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  transmute(Township = TS, State = ST, Variable = VAR_SHORT[var],
            `sfdep's rule` = ehsa_label(sfdep_rule), Corrected = ehsa_label(corrected),
            `Significant hot quarters` = n_hot, `Significant cold quarters` = n_cold) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))

Rule defect. The defect is rare in these data, but where it occurs the label is the opposite of the truth: Mongyang, in the eastern Shan hills, is a significant cold spot of remote violence in 18 of 19 quarters and was labelled an intensifying hot spot. A reader who mapped “intensifying hot spots” as early warnings would have flagged one of the quietest townships in the country.


规则缺陷。 这个缺陷在本数据中很少出现,但一旦出现,标签就与事实正好相反:掸邦 东部山地的勐央,在 19 个季度中有 18 个季度是远程暴力的显著冷点,却被标为增强热点。 如果读者把「增强热点」当作预警来绘图,就会把全国最平静的镇区之一标记出来。



7.3.4 A fourth issue: how many classes would chance produce?第四个问题:偶然会产生多少类别?

The fourth issue is not a defect in code but in how EHSA output is usually read. Each township is tested 19 times, and a single significant hot quarter with no significant cold one is enough to make a township a “sporadic hot spot”. At a threshold that is two-sided 0.10 in effect, that will happen often by chance alone. To see how often, each township’s complete 19-quarter history was moved to a random location, keeping every series and its serial dependence intact and destroying only the spatial arrangement, and the whole analysis was re-run 99 times.


第四个问题不是代码缺陷,而在于 EHSA 输出通常的解读方式。每个镇区要被检验 19 次,只要有一个显著热季度而没有显著冷季度,就足以使其成为 「零星热点」。在实际相当于双侧 0.10 的阈值下,这种情况单凭偶然就会经常发生。为了 知道有多常发生,本研究把每个镇区完整的 19 个季度历史随机移到另一个位置,保持每条 序列及其序列相关不变,只破坏空间排列,然后把整个分析重复 99 次。



Code
EH$null_classes |>
  mutate(class = fct_rev(class)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = class)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = null_lo, xmax = null_hi), colour = "#a8a29e", linewidth = 3.2) +
  geom_point(aes(x = null_mean), colour = "#57534e", size = 1.8) +
  geom_point(aes(x = observed), colour = PAL$conflict, size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(x = pmax(observed, null_hi), label = observed), colour = PAL$conflict,
            hjust = 0, nudge_x = 4, size = 3.1) +
  labs(title = "How many townships each class would hold by chance",
       subtitle = "Red: observed. Grey: 95% range when township histories are placed at random",
       x = "Townships", y = NULL) +
  theme_th(10.5)








Figure 16: Observed number of townships in each class (red) against the range produced by 99 cubes in which township histories were relocated at random (grey bar: 95% interval; grey point: mean). All conflict events.各类别的观测镇区数(红色),与 99 个随机迁移镇区历史的立方体所产生的范围对比(灰条:95% 区间;灰点:均值)。全部冲突事件。






Chance. With no spatial structure at all, about 84 townships would still be classed as sporadic hot spots; the observed 99 is barely above that. The sporadic hot class as a whole is therefore weak evidence, and a township’s label alone says little. What separates a real hot spot from a chance one is how many quarters it spent hot: under the null, fewer than 1% of townships reach 11 or more significant hot quarters. The cold side is the opposite: 28 consecutive and 5 persistent cold spots against fewer than 6 and 1 by chance. And the 80 townships with no pattern are half the chance expectation, because real spatial structure leaves few townships untouched. Fig. 17 therefore maps the number of significant quarters alongside the class.


偶然。 即使完全没有空间结构,也仍会有约 84 个镇区被归为零星热点;观测到的 99 个只是略高于此。 因此,零星热点这个类别整体只是弱证据,单看一个镇区的标签说明不了什么。真正把 真实热点与偶然热点区分开的,是它处于热点状态的季度数:在零模型下,只有不到 1% 的 镇区能达到 11 个或以上的显著热季度。冷的一侧正好相反:观测到 28 个连续冷点与 5 个持续冷点,而偶然情况下分别不到 6 个与 1 个。80 个无模式镇区只有偶然期望的一半,因为 真实的空间结构使很少有镇区不受触及。因此 Fig. 17 在类别旁边同时绘制显著季度数。

Table 15: Townships classed as new, consecutive, intensifying or oscillating hot spots for any variable, with the quarter in which their final run of significant hot quarters began.在任一变量上被归为新出现、连续、增强或振荡热点的镇区,以及其最后一段连续显著热季度开始的季度。





The descriptions below follow the classes of Fig. 17 for all conflict events, drawing on the component variables where they differ. Each is kept within 250 words.


以下描述按 Fig. 17 中全部冲突事件的类别展开,在分项变量有差别时加以引用。 每段不超过 250 词。


Consecutive hot spots (9). These are townships that became significant hot spots and have stayed hot every quarter since. They fall into two groups. The first is the old core of the Dry Zone, across the Sagaing, Magway and Mandalay borders: Myaing, Pakokku, Yesagyo, Salingyi and Singu turned hot in late 2021 and have been hot in 16 or more of the 19 quarters, which is chronic rather than emerging; they miss the “persistent” class only because it requires 90% of quarters. The second group is genuinely new. Chauk and Nyaung-U, on the Ayeyarwady south of the core, have been hot only in the last two quarters, and Pyinoolwin and Kyaukme, on the Mandalay–Lashio road into northern Shan, since mid-2024. Tbl. 15 shows the same direction across variables: the newest runs are in the south and east of the Dry Zone (Meiktila, Kyaukpadaung, Mahlaing and Yenangyaung for violence against civilians, Natogyi for fatalities, Kyaukse for battles), in western Bago and in Mon. The front has been moving south and east, out of the Sagaing plains towards central Myanmar and the roads to Mandalay. These are the townships where conflict is newest and most likely to deepen.


连续热点(9 个)。 这些镇区成为显著热点之后,每个季度都一直保持 热点状态。它们分为两组。第一组是横跨实皆、马圭与曼德勒交界的干燥带老核心:敏建、木各具、耶沙久、 沙林基与新古在 2021 年底转热,在 19 个季度中有 16 个或更多季度是热点,与其说是「新兴」不如说是长期的;它们只是因为「持续」类别要求 90% 的季度,才没有被归入该类。第二组才是真正的新热点:伊洛瓦底江畔、核心以南的稍埠 与良乌只在最近两个季度成为热点,通往掸邦北部的曼德勒–腊戍公路沿线的眉谬与皎梅则从 2024 年中开始。Tbl. 15 显示各变量呈现同一方向:最新的连续热点段出现在干燥带的 南部与东部(针对平民暴力的密铁拉、皎勃东、马莱与仁安羌,死亡人数的纳托吉,战斗的 皎施),以及勃固西部与孟邦。前线一直在向南、向东移动, 从实皆平原移向缅甸中部与通往曼德勒的道路。 这些是冲突最新、也最可能加深的镇区。


Sporadic hot spots (99). This is the largest hot class and the least informative as a label, since chance alone would produce about 84 of them. The count of significant quarters separates two kinds. 23 sporadic hot spots were hot in 11 or more quarters, beyond what chance produces; they are chronic hot spots whose run was broken by one or two quieter quarters, among them Monywa, the township with the most conflict events in the country. They are concentrated in Sagaing (12) and form the body of the Dry Zone cluster found by local Moran’s I. The remaining 76 were hot in fewer quarters; most are in northern Shan, the outer townships of Sagaing, Kachin, Chin, Tanintharyi, Rakhine and Kayah, where conflict came in episodes: an offensive, a lull, another offensive. For these, a single hot quarter should not be over-read, but the episodes are real enough on the ground, and the Markov analysis in § 8 shows that each one raises the risk next door.


零星热点(99 个)。 这是最大的热点类别,作为标签却最缺乏信息量,因为 单凭偶然就会产生约 84 个。 显著季度数把它们分成两类。有 23 个零星热点在 11 个或以上季度 处于热点状态,超出偶然所能产生的程度;它们是长期热点,只是其连续段被一两个较平静 的季度打断,其中包括全国冲突事件最多的镇区蒙育瓦。它们集中在实皆 (12 个),构成局部 Moran’s I 所发现的干燥带聚集的主体。 其余 76 个处于热点状态的季度较少,大多位于掸邦北部、 实皆外围镇区、克钦、钦邦、德林达依、若开与克耶,那里的冲突是阵发式的:一次攻势、 一段平静、再一次攻势。对这些镇区,单个热季度不应被过度解读;但这些阵发在地面上是真实的, § 8 的马尔可夫分析表明,每一次都会提高隔壁的风险。


New, intensifying and oscillating hot spots. These classes are almost empty once the null is corrected. For all conflict events there are 0 new, 0 intensifying and 2 oscillating hot spots. The oscillating ones are informative: Ramree, in Rakhine, was a significant cold spot in 2021–2022 and has been a hot spot in every quarter of 2025 (for battles, since late 2024), as the fighting in Rakhine moved south down the coast; Lawksawk, in southern Shan, was cold in 2023 and hot again from late 2024. Among the component variables, a single new hot spot of battles at Bokpyin in the far south of Tanintharyi, and a new hot spot of violence against civilians at Sidoktaya in Magway, mark places where the latest quarter broke with the past, and Taungtha, south of Myingyan, is the one genuine intensifying hot spot: hot for violence against civilians in 18 of 19 quarters, with a rising trend. The near-absence of these classes is itself a finding: in this conflict, hot spots rarely appear from nowhere, which agrees with the onset analysis in § 8.3.


新出现、增强与振荡热点。 修正零模型之后,这几个类别几乎是空的。就全部冲突事件 而言,新出现热点 0 个、增强热点 0 个、振荡热点 2 个。振荡热点是有信息量的:若开的兰里 在 2021–2022 年是显著冷点,而在 2025 年的每个季度都是热点(战斗方面自 2024 年底起), 因为若开的战事沿海岸向南推进;掸邦南部的罗索在 2023 年是冷点,自 2024 年底起再度转热。 在分项变量中,德林达依最南端博克平的一个战斗新热点,以及马圭锡多达亚的一个针对平民 暴力的新热点,标出了最近一个季度与过去决裂的地方;敏建以南的当达是唯一真正的增强 热点:在 19 个季度中有 18 个季度是针对平民暴力的热点,且趋势上升。这些类别几乎为空, 这本身就是一个发现:在这场冲突中,热点很少凭空出现,这与 § 8.3 的爆发分析 一致。


Consecutive and persistent cold spots (28 and 5). The cold side of the map is far more structured than chance. The persistent cold spots are Kengtung, Mongyang and Mongping in eastern Shan, and Narphan and Mongmao in the Wa self-administered area: significant cold spots in 18 or 19 of 19 quarters. The consecutive cold spots are two groups with different histories. 9 are in the same eastern and southern Shan hills and the Wa area, cold almost throughout. 17 are in Yangon, and their tau is negative: Yangon was not a cold spot in 2021, when urban bombings and the crackdown kept it active, and its townships turned cold one after another from the second half of 2022. For the eastern Shan hills the cold reflects a region largely outside the war, under armed groups that stayed out of it, though thin reporting may contribute (§ 4). For Yangon it reflects the suppression of the urban resistance, not the absence of the state’s violence.


连续冷点与持续冷点(28 个与 5 个)。 地图冷的一侧远比 偶然情况更有结构。持续冷点是掸邦东部的景栋、勐央与勐平,以及佤自治区的纳潘与勐冒: 它们在 19 个季度中有 18 或 19 个季度是显著冷点。连续冷点是历史不同的两组。有 9 个 位于同一片掸邦东部与南部山地以及佤地区,几乎始终是冷点。另有 17 个在仰光,而它们的 tau 为负:2021 年仰光并不是冷点,当时城市爆炸袭击与镇压使其保持 活跃;从 2022 年下半年起,其各镇区相继转为冷点。对掸邦东部山地而言,冷意味着一个基本处于战争之外、由置身事外的 武装团体控制的区域,尽管报道稀少也可能有影响(§ 4)。对仰光而言,冷反映的是 城市抵抗力量被镇压,而不是国家暴力的缺席。


Sporadic cold spots (105) and no pattern (80). Sporadic cold spots are led by Ayeyarwady (20), Yangon (18), Shan (South) (14), Magway (12). They are townships that have been significantly quiet relative to the country in some quarters, most of them in the delta, around Yangon, in southern Shan and in the south of Magway and western Bago. The last two deserve attention: they were significantly quiet in 2021–2023, and since 2024 Tbl. 15 finds new hot spots of violence against civilians there (Minhla, Letpadan, Okpho and Monyo in western Bago; Yenangyaung and Sidoktaya in Magway). A township that was sporadically cold is not necessarily safe. The 80 townships with no detectable pattern were never significant in either direction. They are not “average” in a reassuring sense: they include three of the five townships with the most conflict events in the country, Kawkareik, Kale and Hpakant, whose neighbourhoods were never extreme relative to the rest of the country in the same quarter (§ 9).


零星冷点(105 个)与无模式(80 个)。 零星冷点居前的是 Ayeyarwady (20), Yangon (18), Shan (South) (14), Magway (12)。它们是在某些季度相对于全国显著平静的镇区,大多位于三角洲、 仰光周边、掸邦南部,以及马圭南部与勃固西部。后两者值得注意:它们在 2021–2023 年显著平静,而自 2024 年起 Tbl. 15 在那里发现了针对平民暴力的新热点(勃固西部的 敏拉、勒巴丹、奥波与茂良;马圭的仁安羌与锡多达亚)。一个曾经零星冷的镇区未必安全。 80 个未检测到模式的镇区,在任何方向上都从未显著。它们并不是令人安心意义上 的「一般」:其中包括全国冲突事件最多的五个镇区中的三个,即高加力、葛礼与帕敢,它们的 邻域在同一季度相对于全国其他地区从未极端到显著的程度(§ 9)。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
text:
7.6 Sensitivity敏感性

Each alternative changes one choice relative to the primary run (quarterly cube, one quarter of time lag, queen contiguity, folded p ≤ 0.05) and counts how many townships keep the same class, and how many stay on the same side (hot, cold or neither).


每个备选方案都只相对主分析(季度立方体、一个季度的时间滞后、queen 邻接、折叠 p ≤ 0.05)改变一项选择,并统计有多少镇区保持相同类别,以及有多少镇区停留在同一侧 (热、冷或都不是)。



Code
EH$sens |>
  mutate(ord = match(spec, c("Primary (quarterly, k = 1, queen, folded p)",
                             "Two-sided p ≤ 0.05", "k = 0 (no time lag)",

                             "Monthly cube (57 months)"))) |>

  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))

Table 16: Sensitivity of the EHSA classification of all conflict events.全部冲突事件 EHSA 分类的敏感性。





Sensitivity. The side a township falls on is robust; the exact class is less so. Changing the time lag keeps 310 of 329 townships on the same side with \(k = 2\) and 301 with \(k = 0\). The neighbour definition and the time unit matter more: with six nearest neighbours or a monthly cube, between a quarter and a third of townships change class, mostly between sporadic and no pattern at the edges of the clusters. Requiring a two-sided p ≤ 0.05 moves 52 townships into “no pattern”; 49 of them were sporadic hot or cold spots, and 39 had only one or two significant quarters, which is the group § 7.3.4 already identified as weak. One assumption deserves a warning. The Mann-Kendall test assumes independent observations, but with \(k = 1\) consecutive Gi* values share a quarter of data; the median lag-1 autocorrelation of the series is 0.64 (0.51 with \(k = 0\)). Positive autocorrelation makes the trend test too liberal (Hamed & Rao, 1998), so the trend-based classes (intensifying, diminishing) should be read with caution. Here they are almost empty, so the practical consequence is small.


敏感性。 镇区落在哪一侧是稳健的;具体类别则不那么稳健。改变时间滞后时, \(k = 2\) 下 329 个镇区中有 310 个保持在同一侧, \(k = 0\) 下有 301 个。 邻居定义与时间单元的影响更大:使用六个最近邻或月度立方体时,四分之一到三分之一的镇区 改变类别,大多是在聚集边缘于零星与无模式之间变动。要求双侧 p ≤ 0.05 会使 52 个镇区转入「无模式」;其中 49 个原为零星热点或冷点,39 个只有一两个显著季度,也就是 § 7.3.4 已经判断为弱证据的那一组。有一个假设值得警示:Mann-Kendall 检验假定 观测相互独立,但在 \(k = 1\) 时相邻的 Gi* 值共享一个季度的数据;序列的滞后一阶自相关 中位数为 0.64 (\(k = 0\) 时为 0.51)。 正自相关会使趋势检验过于宽松 (Hamed & Rao, 1998),因此基于趋势的类别(增强、减弱)应谨慎 解读。这里它们几乎为空,所以实际影响很小。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
section: 8.1 A spatial Markov chain空间马尔可夫链
text:
8.1 A spatial Markov chain空间马尔可夫链

Each township-quarter is assigned one of four states by its number of conflict events: None (0), Sporadic (1–3, about one a month or fewer), Sustained (4–14, up to about one a week) and Intense (15 or more). The cut points are round numbers close to the quartiles of the pooled distribution, and they read as an operational scale. A township’s neighbourhood is assigned a state in the same way, from the average count of its queen neighbours in the same quarter. The 5,922 quarter-to-quarter transitions are then tabulated twice: once pooled, and once separately for each neighbourhood state. If conflict does not spread, the four conditional matrices should all look like the pooled one.


每个镇区-季度按其冲突事件数被赋予四种状态之一:无(0)、零星(1–3 起,约每月 一起或更少)、持续(4–14 起,最多约每周一起)与激烈(15 起或以上)。切分点是 接近合并分布四分位数的整数,可以当作一种操作性的量表来读。镇区的邻域也以同样 方式赋予状态,依据是同一季度其 queen 邻居的平均计数。然后把 5,922 次季度间转移制成两种表:一张合并表,以及按邻域状态分开的 四张条件表。如果冲突不扩散,四张条件矩阵就应当都与合并矩阵相似。



Code
S  <- matrix(as.integer(to_state(X)), nrow(X))   # own state, township x quarter
L  <- apply(X, 2, function(x) lag.listw(lw, x))  # neighbourhood mean
SL <- matrix(as.integer(to_state(L)), nrow(X))   # neighbourhood state

trans <- tibble(from = as.vector(S[, -TT]), to = as.vector(S[, -1]),
                lag  = as.vector(SL[, -TT]))
P_cond <- lapply(1:4, function(l) row_prob(count_mat(trans$from[trans$lag == l],
                                                     trans$to[trans$lag == l])))




Code
st_lab <- MK$markov$states
mk_df <- map_dfr(seq_along(st_lab), function(l) {
  P <- MK$markov$P_cond[[l]]; N <- MK$markov$N_cond[[l]]
  expand_grid(from = seq_along(st_lab), to = seq_along(st_lab)) |>
    mutate(p = P[cbind(from, to)], n_row = rowSums(N)[from],
           panel = sprintf("Neighbours: %s (n = %s)", st_lab[l], n_fmt(sum(N))),
           panel_i = l)
}) |>
  mutate(from = factor(st_lab[from], levels = rev(st_lab)),
         to = factor(st_lab[to], levels = st_lab),
         panel = fct_reorder(panel, panel_i))

ggplot(mk_df, aes(to, from, fill = p)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n_row > 0, sprintf("%.2f", p), "–"),
                colour = p > 0.45), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#fff7f3", "#fa9fb5", "#c51b8a", "#49006a"),
                       limits = c(0, 1), name = "P(to | from)") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "#1c1917"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Where a township goes next quarter depends on its neighbours",
       x = "State next quarter", y = "State this quarter") +
  theme_th(9.5) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "right")








Figure 20: Quarter-to-quarter transition probabilities between conflict states, by the state of the township’s neighbourhood at the start of the quarter. Each row sums to one. The number of transitions in each panel is given in its title.冲突状态的季度间转移概率,按季度初镇区邻域的状态分列。每一行之和为 1。各子图标题中给出该子图的转移次数。






Transitions. Read the top row of each panel, the fate of a quiet township. With quiet neighbours it stays quiet the next quarter with probability 0.75; with neighbours in intense conflict, only 0.48. A sporadic township escalates to sustained or intense conflict with probability 0.16 beside quiet neighbours and 0.55 beside intense ones. And an intense township stays intense with probability 0.58 in a sporadic neighbourhood but 0.77 in an intense one. Every step up the neighbourhood scale shifts probability towards escalation and persistence. Translated into time, a quiet township in a quiet neighbourhood waits on average 4.1 quarters before its first event; in an intense neighbourhood, 1.9.


转移。 先看每个子图的第一行,即一个平静镇区的去向。邻居平静时,它下一季度保持 平静的概率为 0.75;邻居处于激烈冲突时,只有 0.48。零星镇区在平静邻居旁升级为持续或激烈冲突的 概率是 0.16,在激烈邻居旁则是 0.55。 激烈镇区在零星邻域中保持激烈的概率是 0.58,在激烈邻域中则是 0.77。邻域每上升一级,概率就向升级与持续倾斜。换算成时间: 平静邻域中的平静镇区平均要等待 4.1 个季度 才出现第一起事件;在激烈邻域中只需 1.9 个季度。


8.1.1 Is the difference real?差异是真实的吗?

The standard test is a likelihood ratio of the conditional matrices against the pooled one (Bickenbach & Bode, 2003), which gives \(Q = 382.7\) on 36 degrees of freedom. Its chi-square reference assumes that transitions are independent, and these are not: the same township appears in 18 consecutive transitions, and neighbours share shocks. A permutation null that does not need the assumption is therefore used as well. Each township is given the neighbourhood history of a randomly chosen township, which keeps every township’s own sequence of states and every neighbourhood’s sequence of states intact, including the nationwide surge of 2021–2023, and breaks only the pairing between a township and its real neighbours.


标准检验是条件矩阵对合并矩阵的似然比检验 (Bickenbach & Bode, 2003),得到 \(Q = 382.7\),自由度为 36。其卡方参照分布 假定各次转移相互独立,而事实并非如此:同一个镇区出现在 18 次连续转移中,相邻镇区 也共享冲击。因此本研究同时使用一个不依赖该假设的置换零模型:给每个镇区分配一个 随机选取的镇区的邻域历史。这样每个镇区自身的状态序列、每个邻域的状态序列(包括 2021–2023 年的全国性激增)都保持不变,被打破的只是镇区与其真实邻居之间的配对。



Code
h1 <- tibble(Q = MK$markov$perm_Q) |>
  ggplot(aes(Q)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#d6d3d1", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = MK$markov$Q, colour = PAL$conflict, linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = MK$markov$Q, y = Inf, vjust = 1.4, hjust = 1.05, size = 3.2,
           label = sprintf("observed Q = %.0f", MK$markov$Q), colour = PAL$conflict) +
  labs(title = "Likelihood-ratio statistic", x = "Q", y = "Permutations") +
  theme_th(10)

h2 <- tibble(C = MK$markov$perm_C) |>
  ggplot(aes(C)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#d6d3d1", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = MK$markov$C_obs, colour = PAL$conflict, linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = MK$markov$C_obs, y = Inf, vjust = 1.4, hjust = 1.05, size = 3.2,
           label = sprintf("observed = %+.2f", MK$markov$C_obs), colour = PAL$conflict) +
  labs(title = "Onset contrast", x = "Difference in probability", y = NULL) +
  theme_th(10)

h1 | h2








Figure 21: Permutation distributions (999 draws) of the likelihood-ratio statistic and of the onset contrast, with the observed values in red. The onset contrast is the probability that a quiet township sees conflict next quarter with sustained or intense neighbours, minus the same probability with quiet neighbours.似然比统计量与爆发对比量的置换分布(999 次抽取),红线为观测值。爆发对比量 = 邻居处于持续或激烈状态时平静镇区下一季度出现冲突的概率,减去邻居平静时的同一概率。






Against the null. No permuted pairing comes close to the observed values. The likelihood ratio is far beyond every permutation (permutation p = 0.001, the smallest 999 draws can give), and so is the onset contrast: +0.25 observed, against a permutation mean of -0.06. The null mean is slightly negative, which is informative in itself: a quiet township paired with a random busy neighbourhood is, if anything, a little less likely to see conflict, because busy neighbourhoods are concentrated in the busy years and quiet townships in the quiet ones. The observed positive contrast is therefore not the national trend, which the permutation preserves. It is the real neighbours.


与零模型对比。 没有任何一次置换配对接近观测值。似然比远超所有置换值(置换 p = 0.001,即 999 次抽取所能给出的最小值),爆发 对比量也一样:观测值 +0.25,置换均值 -0.06。零模型均值略为负,这本身就有信息量: 把平静镇区与一个随机的繁忙邻域配对时,它出现冲突的可能性反而略低,因为繁忙邻域 集中在繁忙的年份,平静镇区集中在平静的年份。因此观测到的正对比并不是置换所保留的 全国趋势,而是真实邻居的作用。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
section: 8.2 Spillover or shared geography?溢出效应,还是共同的地理条件?
text:
8.2 Spillover or shared geography?溢出效应,还是共同的地理条件?

The Markov result has an obvious alternative explanation that the permutation does not remove. Some regions are violent throughout, for reasons of terrain, history or who controls them, so a township in such a region has violent neighbours and a high propensity of its own, and would escalate more often even if nothing crossed township lines. A logit model of escalation with township fixed effects removes that explanation: each township is compared only with itself in other quarters, so every permanent difference between townships drops out. Quarter fixed effects remove nationwide shocks. What is left for the neighbourhood term is whether a township escalates more often in the quarters after its own neighbourhood has been more violent than usual. Standard errors are clustered by township.


马尔可夫结果有一个明显的替代解释,置换并不能排除它。有些地区始终暴力,原因可能是 地形、历史或控制者,所以这类地区的镇区既有暴力的邻居,也有较高的自身倾向, 即使没有任何东西跨越镇区边界,它也会更常升级。带镇区固定效应的升级 logit 模型 可以排除这一解释:每个镇区只与它自己在其他季度的状况相比,镇区之间一切永久性的 差异都被消去。季度固定效应则消去全国性冲击。剩下给邻域项的,是:当一个镇区 自己的邻域比平常更暴力之后,它是否更常升级。标准误按镇区聚类。



Code
esc <- trans |>
  filter(from < 4) |>                                  # can still escalate
  mutate(escalate = as.integer(to > from), lag_log = log1p(lag_n),
         from_f = factor(STATES[from]), TS_f = factor(TS_PCODE), t_f = factor(t))

fit_fe <- glm(escalate ~ lag_log + from_f + t_f + TS_f, data = esc,
              family = binomial)
coeftest(fit_fe, vcov. = vcovCL(fit_fe, cluster = ~ TS_PCODE, type = "HC0"))




Code
MK$fe |>
  transmute(Model = model, `Odds ratio` = OR, `95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f – %.2f", lo, hi),
            p = pv(p), `Township-quarters` = n) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(`Odds ratio`, decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_number(`Township-quarters`, decimals = 0) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13))

Table 17: Odds ratio of escalating next quarter per one-unit increase in log(1 + neighbourhood mean events), with 95% confidence intervals from township-clustered standard errors. All models control for the township’s own current state.邻域平均事件数取 log(1 + x) 后每增加一个单位,下一季度升级的优势比,95% 置信区间基于按镇区聚类的标准误。所有模型都控制了镇区自身的当前状态。





Fixed effects. The neighbourhood effect does not shrink when the alternative explanations are removed; it grows, from an odds ratio of 1.80 with no fixed effects to 2.43 with both. On the probability scale, the full model puts the average chance that a quiet township sees conflict next quarter at 25% when its neighbours recorded nothing this quarter and 64% when they averaged 15 events. That the estimate rises once permanent differences are removed suggests the pooled model was diluted by stable regions, such as the eastern Shan hills, where neighbours are quiet and the township is quiet, and nothing changes. The model is still observational: an unmeasured shock that reaches a township’s neighbours one quarter before the township itself would produce the same pattern. But that shock would itself be a form of spread.


固定效应。 排除替代解释之后,邻域效应并没有缩小,反而增大:优势比从不含固定 效应时的 1.80 升至同时含两种固定效应时的 2.43。换算成概率,完整模型估计:邻居本季度没有任何事件时, 平静镇区下一季度出现冲突的平均概率为 25%; 邻居平均有 15 起事件时为 64%。估计值在消去 永久性差异后上升,说明合并模型被稳定区域稀释了,例如掸邦东部山地:那里邻居平静、 镇区平静,一切都没有变化。这个模型仍然是观察性的:一个先于镇区本身一个季度到达其 邻居的未观测冲击也会产生同样的模式。但这样的冲击本身就是一种扩散。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
section: 8.3 When does a township first enter the conflict?一个镇区何时首次卷入冲突?
text:
8.3 When does a township first enter the conflict?一个镇区何时首次卷入冲突?

The Markov chain and the fixed-effects model describe escalation in townships already exposed. A different question is how conflict reached each township in the first place. A township’s onset is defined as the first quarter in which it records four or more events, the threshold of sustained conflict. An onset is adjacent if at least one queen neighbour had its onset in an earlier quarter, and a jump otherwise. If conflict reached townships by spreading outwards, adjacent onsets should be more common than if the same onset dates had been dealt to townships at random. The null keeps the townships already in sustained conflict in 2021 Q1 and those that never reached it, and shuffles the dates among the 261 townships whose onset falls inside the window.


马尔可夫链与固定效应模型描述的是已暴露镇区的升级。另一个问题是,冲突最初是如何 到达每个镇区的。镇区的爆发定义为它首次记录到四起及以上事件(即持续冲突门槛)的 季度。如果至少有一个 queen 邻居在更早的季度已经爆发,则称为相邻爆发,否则称为 跳跃爆发。如果冲突是向外扩散到达各镇区的,那么相邻爆发应比「同样的爆发日期被 随机分配给各镇区」时更常见。零模型保留 2021 年第一季度已处于持续冲突的镇区与从未 达到该门槛的镇区不变,只在爆发时间位于窗口之内的 261 个镇区之间 打乱日期。



Code
on_sf <- ts_an |> select(TS_PCODE) |>
  left_join(MK$onset$table, by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  mutate(when = case_when(type == "Never sustained" ~ "Never",
                          type == "Sustained from 2021 Q1" ~ "2021 Q1",
                          TRUE ~ as.character(year(onset))),
         when = factor(when, levels = c("2021 Q1", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024", "2025", "Never")))

on_cols <- c("2021 Q1" = "#49006a", "2021" = "#ae017e", "2022" = "#f768a1",
             "2023" = "#fbb4b9", "2024" = "#fde0dd", "2025" = "#fff7f3", "Never" = "#e7e5e4")

m_on <- map_base(
  list(geom_sf(data = on_sf, aes(fill = when), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05),
       geom_sf(data = on_sf |> filter(type == "Jump onset"), fill = NA,
               colour = "#1c1917", linewidth = 0.45)),
  title = "First quarter of sustained conflict",
  subtitle = "Outlined: jump onsets, with no neighbour in sustained conflict before",
  state_lw = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual("Onset", values = on_cols, drop = FALSE)

h_on <- tibble(s = MK$onset$null) |>
  ggplot(aes(s)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#d6d3d1", colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = MK$onset$share_obs, colour = PAL$conflict, linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Adjacent onsets vs random timing",
       subtitle = sprintf("Observed %s, permutation p = %.2f",
                          pct(100 * MK$onset$share_obs), MK$onset$p),
       x = "Share of onsets that are adjacent", y = "Permutations") +
  theme_th(10)

m_on + h_on + plot_layout(widths = c(1.15, 1))








Figure 22: Left: the year in which each township first recorded four or more conflict events in a quarter, with jump onsets (no neighbour in sustained conflict before) outlined. Right: the share of adjacent onsets against 999 random reassignments of the same onset dates.左:各镇区首次在一个季度内记录到四起及以上冲突事件的年份,跳跃爆发(此前没有邻居处于持续冲突)加粗描边。右:相邻爆发占比与同样爆发日期的 999 次随机重分配对比。






Onsets. 74.3% of onsets are adjacent, and random timing produces about 72.2%; the difference is not significant (p = 0.11). The map shows why. 174 of the 261 onsets inside the window happened in 2021, within three quarters of the coup, in every one of MIMU’s 18 state and region units, led by Yangon (31), Sagaing (27), Mandalay (22). When most of the country ignites at once, almost any onset is next to an earlier one, and timing carries little spatial information. The jump onsets are all early: 64 in 2021 and 3 in 2022. After that the pattern is unambiguous. All 38 onsets from 2023 onwards were adjacent to a township already in sustained conflict. The 42 townships that never reached sustained conflict are led by Shan (East) (8), Yangon (7), Ayeyarwady (6).


爆发。 74.3% 的爆发是相邻爆发,随机时间分配约产生 72.2%;差异不显著(p = 0.11)。 地图说明了原因。窗口内的 261 次爆发中,有 174 次发生在 2021 年,即政变后三个季度之内,遍及全部 18 个省邦,居前的是 Yangon (31), Sagaing (27), Mandalay (22):这是一场全国性的浪潮。 当全国大部分地区同时燃起时,几乎任何一次爆发都紧挨着更早的爆发,时间就几乎不携带 空间信息。跳跃爆发全部发生在早期:2021 年 64 次, 2022 年 3 次。此后格局就很清楚了:2023 年以后的全部 38 次爆发,都与一个已处于持续冲突的镇区相邻。从未达到持续冲突的 42 个镇区中,居前的是 Shan (East)(8)、Yangon(7)、Ayeyarwady(6)。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
section: 8.4 What the value-added analysis adds附加价值分析补充了什么
text:
8.4 What the value-added analysis adds附加价值分析补充了什么

The three analyses separate two processes that the hot spot maps run together. Onset was a national shock: the uprising after the coup broke out across the country within months, with no single source from which it spread, and the timing of first onsets is no more clustered than chance. Escalation is contagious: once conflict exists, a township’s next quarter depends strongly on its neighbours, beyond its own history, beyond any permanent regional propensity, and beyond the nationwide trend. Since 2023, conflict has entered new townships only from next door. For RQ3 the answer is therefore escalation, not onset. The practical consequence, taken up in § 10, is that the edge of an active zone is predictable from one quarter to the next.
Assumptions and limitations. The states discretise counts, and the thresholds are a choice; queen contiguity defines “neighbour”, so spread along a road between non-adjacent townships is invisible. The chi-square test ignores dependence, which is why the permutation test is the one relied on. The fixed-effects logit with 18 quarters per township is subject to some incidental-parameter bias, and is observational.


三项分析把热点地图混在一起的两个过程区分开来。爆发是一场全国性冲击:政变后的 起义在数月之内就遍及全国,并没有一个单一的扩散源,首次爆发的时间也不比随机情况更 聚集。升级则具有传染性:一旦冲突存在,一个镇区下一季度的状况就强烈依赖于其邻居, 这种依赖超出其自身历史、超出任何永久性的区域倾向,也超出全国趋势。2023 年以来, 冲突只从隔壁进入新的镇区。因此,对 RQ3 的回答是升级,而非爆发。其实际意义 (见 § 10)在于:活跃区域的边缘在季度之间是可以预测的。
假设与局限。 状态是对计数的离散化,阈值是一种选择;queen 邻接定义了「邻居」, 因此沿道路在不相邻镇区之间的扩散是看不见的。卡方检验忽略了相依性,所以本研究依赖 的是置换检验。每个镇区 18 个季度的固定效应 logit 存在一定的伴随参数偏误,而且是 观察性的。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
section: 9.1 What the methods say together各方法合起来说明了什么
text:
9.1 What the methods say together各方法合起来说明了什么

Each method answers a narrower question than the one a reader brings to a conflict map, and the answers are most useful read together. Tbl. 18 lines them up for the regions that recur through the report.


每种方法回答的问题都比读者面对冲突地图时心中的问题更窄,把它们放在一起读才最有用。 Tbl. 18 把各方法对报告中反复出现的地区的结论并列在一起。

Table 18: Synthesis by region. LISA and Gi* refer to the whole-period totals of all conflict events; EHSA to the period-conditional classification; diffusion to the onset and Markov analysis.按地区的综合。LISA 与 Gi* 指全部冲突事件的整期总量;EHSA 指按期条件化的分类;扩散指爆发与马尔可夫分析。





Three conclusions follow.
The geography of the war has a stable core and moving edges. The Dry Zone, where the post-coup resistance was strongest among the Bamar majority, is the centre of the conflict on every measure and every year to 2023, and remains a chronic hot spot. What moves are the edges: south and east from the core towards central Myanmar and the Mandalay–Lashio road, and the separate fronts in Rakhine, northern Shan and the south-east, which opened at different times. That is why global Moran’s I fell after 2023 even though total violence did not: the conflict became less concentrated, not less intense.
Hot spots grow from existing hot spots. The EHSA finds almost no hot spot appearing from nowhere, and the value-added analysis gives the reason: after the nationwide outbreak of 2021, conflict entered new townships only from next door, and escalation in any township depends strongly on its neighbours. The new consecutive hot spots on the edges of the Dry Zone are the visible result of that process.
Calm is not uniform. The persistent cold zone of the eastern Shan hills and the newer cold zone of Yangon look alike on a map and mean opposite things. The first is a region that has largely stayed out of the war. The second is a city where the resistance was put down.


由此得出三个结论。
战争的地理格局有一个稳定的核心和不断移动的边缘。 干燥带是政变后缅族抵抗最强的 地方,在 2023 年之前的每一年、每一项指标上都是冲突的中心,至今仍是长期热点。移动的 是边缘:从核心向南、向东移向缅甸中部与曼德勒–腊戍公路;以及在不同时间打开的若开、 掸邦北部与东南方向的几条独立前线。这解释了为何 2023 年后全局 Moran’s I 下降而暴力 总量并未下降:冲突变得不那么集中,而不是不那么激烈。
热点从已有的热点中生长出来。 EHSA 几乎没有发现凭空出现的热点,附加价值分析给出了 原因:在 2021 年的全国性爆发之后,冲突只从隔壁进入新的镇区,而任何镇区的升级都 强烈依赖于其邻居。干燥带边缘那些新的连续热点,正是这一过程的可见结果。
平静并不均一。 掸邦东部山地的持续冷区与仰光较新的冷区在地图上看起来一样,含义 却相反。前者是一个基本置身于战争之外的地区;后者是一座抵抗力量被镇压的城市。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
section: 9.2 What neighbourhood statistics cannot see邻域统计量看不见什么
text:
9.2 What neighbourhood statistics cannot see邻域统计量看不见什么

Three of the five townships with the most conflict events, Kawkareik, Kale and Hpakant, are not significant under local Moran’s I or Gi*, and their EHSA class is “no pattern detected”. Each is a high-conflict township whose neighbours are much quieter. Local Moran’s I could in principle flag them as High-Low outliers, but with only five or six neighbours, a single extreme township among moderate ones does not reach significance. Gi* sums the neighbourhood, so one township’s events are diluted by its neighbours’. This is a property of the methods, not an error, and it means a hot spot map must not be read as a list of the most violent places. For operational use the cluster maps should always be read alongside the count maps of § 5.


冲突事件最多的五个镇区中,有三个,即高加力、葛礼与帕敢,在局部 Moran’s I 与 Gi* 下 都不显著,EHSA 类别也是「未检测到模式」。它们每一个都是冲突很高、而邻居要平静得多的 镇区。局部 Moran’s I 原则上可以把它们标为「高-低」异常值,但只有五六个邻居时,一个 处于中等邻居之间的极端镇区达不到显著性。Gi* 对邻域求和,所以一个镇区的事件会被 邻居稀释。这是方法本身的性质,并非错误;但它意味着热点地图不能被读成「最暴力 地点」的名单。在实际应用中,聚集地图应当始终与 § 5 的计数地图一起阅读。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
section: 9.3 Geovisualisation and geocommunication choices地理可视化与地理传达的选择
text:
9.3 Geovisualisation and geocommunication choices地理可视化与地理传达的选择

The figures follow a few rules, chosen so that a reader who skips the text can still read the maps correctly.

One colour, one meaning. Red is always more conflict or a hot spot, blue always less or a cold spot, and the same palette is used for the same statistic everywhere: the LISA quadrants, the Gi* classes and the EHSA classes each have one fixed colour scheme (R/utils.R). In the LISA maps the outlier quadrants are paler than the cluster quadrants, so an outlier is not mistaken for a cluster.
Significance is shown, not implied. Non-significant townships are pale grey, and townships that survive FDR correction carry a heavy outline, so the strength of evidence is visible on the map itself. In the EHSA maps “no pattern detected” is left blank, since it is not a result.
Comparison by small multiples. Variables, years and specifications are compared in panels that share classes, which keeps differences between panels meaningful.
Counts beside statistics. Every local statistic map has a count map to set against it (§ 5), and the heat strip of Fig. 7 shows the raw space-time cube that EHSA summarises.
Captions that state the reading. Each commentary block names the conclusion first, in bold, and then the evidence for it.



本报告的图形遵循几条规则,目的是让跳过正文的读者也能正确读图。

一种颜色,一种含义。 红色始终表示冲突更多或热点,蓝色始终表示冲突更少或冷点; 同一统计量在各处使用同一调色板:LISA 象限、Gi* 类别与 EHSA 类别各有一套固定配色 (见 R/utils.R)。在 LISA 地图中,异常值象限比聚集象限颜色更浅,避免把异常值 误读为聚集。
显著性被显示,而不是被暗示。 不显著的镇区为浅灰色,通过 FDR 校正的镇区加粗 描边,因此证据强度直接体现在地图上。EHSA 地图中「未检测到模式」留白,因为它不是 一个结果。
用小多图做比较。 变量、年份与设定都在共享分级的子图中比较,使子图之间的差异 有意义。
统计量旁附计数。 每一幅局部统计量地图都有一幅计数地图可供对照(§ 5), Fig. 7 的热力条带则展示了 EHSA 所概括的原始时空立方体。
说明直接给出读法。 每段解读先以粗体点明结论,再给出证据。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
text:
10.1 Anticipate the edges预判边缘

The most actionable result is the contagion of escalation (§ 8). If a township’s next quarter depends on its neighbours, the townships most likely to see conflict next are the ones that are still quiet but border intense fighting. This is testable. Transition matrices estimated only on data to the end of 2024 were used to predict which quiet or sporadic townships would reach sustained conflict in the next quarter, through 2025.


最具可操作性的结果是升级的传染性(§ 8)。如果一个镇区下一季度的状况取决于其 邻居,那么接下来最可能出现冲突的,就是那些仍然平静、却与激烈战斗相邻的镇区。这一点 可以检验:本研究只用截至 2024 年底的数据估计转移矩阵,然后预测在 2025 年各季度中, 哪些平静或零星镇区会在下一季度进入持续冲突。

Code
ol <- ts_an |> select(TS_PCODE, TS, ST) |> left_join(MK$outlook, by = "TS_PCODE")
edge <- ol |> filter(own <= 2, lag == 4)
map_base(
  list(geom_sf(data = ol, aes(fill = p_next), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.05),
       geom_sf(data = edge, fill = NA, colour = "#1c1917", linewidth = 0.6)),
  title = "Where sustained conflict is likely next quarter",
  subtitle = "Probability of 4+ events in 2025 Q4; outlined: quiet or sporadic townships beside intense ones") +
  scale_fill_gradientn("P(4+ events)", colours = c("#fafaf9", "#fde0dd", "#f768a1", "#ae017e", "#49006a"),
                       limits = c(0, 1), labels = label_percent())








Figure 23: Outlook for 2025 Q4: the probability that each township is in sustained or intense conflict (four or more events) next quarter, from its own state and its neighbourhood’s state in 2025 Q3 and the transition matrices of Fig. 20. Outlined: townships that were only quiet or sporadic in 2025 Q3 but whose neighbourhood was intense, the edge where escalation is most likely.2025 年第四季度展望:依据 2025 年第三季度镇区自身与其邻域的状态,以及 Fig. 20 的转移矩阵,估计各镇区下一季度处于持续或激烈冲突(四起及以上事件)的概率。描边:2025 年第三季度自身仅为平静或零星、但邻域处于激烈冲突的镇区,即最可能升级的边缘。






The edge. Adding the neighbourhood raises the AUC of the forecast from 0.71 to 0.83 on quarters the model had not seen, which is a substantial gain from a rule that needs nothing but last quarter’s counts. Applied to the latest quarter, 20 townships were quiet or sporadic in 2025 Q3 but bordered by intense conflict. The 13 sporadic ones have a probability of about 55% of sustained conflict the next quarter (Bawlake, Bokpyin, Gangaw, Hlaingbwe, Homalin, Kyaukpadaung, Mabein, Mogaung, Mongmit, Myaung, Namhsan, Saw, Tabayin), and the 7 quiet ones about 20% (Hkamti, Htantabin, Kyaukse, Lawksawk, Momauk, Pyinoolwin, Ramree). They are the places where protection of civilians, pre-positioned humanitarian supplies and monitoring would act before the violence arrives rather than after. Because the rule uses only counts that ACLED publishes weekly, it can be refreshed every quarter at almost no cost.


边缘。 在模型未见过的季度上,加入邻域信息使预测的 AUC 从 0.71 提高到 0.83; 一条只需要上一季度计数的规则能带来这样的提升,相当可观。把它用于最近一个季度:有 20 个镇区在 2025 年第三季度自身平静或零星,却与激烈冲突相邻。其中 13 个零星镇区下一季度进入持续冲突的概率约为 55%(Bawlake、Bokpyin、Gangaw、Hlaingbwe、Homalin、Kyaukpadaung、Mabein、Mogaung、Mongmit、Myaung、Namhsan、Saw、Tabayin), 7 个平静镇区约为 20% (Hkamti、Htantabin、Kyaukse、Lawksawk、Momauk、Pyinoolwin、Ramree)。在这些地方,平民保护、人道物资预置与监测 可以在暴力到来之前而不是之后发挥作用。由于这条规则只用到 ACLED 每周发布的计数, 它可以每个季度以几乎为零的成本更新。

title: Take-home Exercise 2: Geospatial Analytics for Peace课后作业二：面向和平的地理空间分析
text:
10.2 Other implications其他启示

Protect civilians where violence against them is moving. Violence against civilians is the most concentrated variable, almost entirely inside the Dry Zone, and it is initiated mainly by state forces. Its newest consecutive hot spots (Tbl. 15) are in the south of the Dry Zone and in western Bago, where the conflict has been spreading. Documentation, protection and humanitarian access efforts that are organised around the Sagaing core may need to extend south.
Plan for remote violence. Explosions and remote violence have become the largest category and, by 2025, overwhelmingly the military’s. Their hot spots extend into the south-east, beyond the battle front. For civilians, the relevant risk map is therefore wider than the map of fighting, and early warning, shelter and medical capacity need to be planned against it.
Read the cold spots carefully. The eastern Shan hills and the Wa area are persistent cold spots, and the delta and Yangon are increasingly cold. The first may be the most promising ground for local ceasefires and the return of displaced people. Yangon’s cold status, on the other hand, follows the suppression of resistance, not a settlement, and a cold spot of recorded events is not proof of safety where reporting is thin.
Monitor rather than map once. The geography has changed every year. Because the whole pipeline is reproducible (§ 12), the cube, the EHSA and the outlook can be refreshed as each quarter of ACLED data arrives, turning a one-off analysis into routine monitoring.


在针对平民的暴力移动之处保护平民。 针对平民的暴力是最集中的变量,几乎完全位于 干燥带之内,且主要由国家武装力量发起。它最新的连续热点(Tbl. 15)位于干燥带 南部与勃固西部,也就是冲突正在扩散的方向。围绕实皆核心组织的记录、保护与人道准入 工作,可能需要向南延伸。
为远程暴力做准备。 爆炸与远程暴力已成为最大的类别,到 2025 年绝大多数来自军方。 其热点延伸到东南,超出了战斗前线。因此对平民而言,相关的风险地图比战斗地图更宽, 预警、避难与医疗能力需要据此规划。
谨慎解读冷点。 掸邦东部山地与佤地区是持续冷点,三角洲与仰光则越来越冷。前者或许 是地方停火与流离失所者返乡最有希望的地方。而仰光的「冷」源于抵抗力量被镇压,而非 达成和解;在报道稀少的地方,「记录在案的事件」很少,并不能证明安全。
持续监测,而不是一次性制图。 冲突的地理格局每年都在变化。由于整个流程是可复现的 (§ 12),时空立方体、EHSA 与展望都可以随着每个季度 ACLED 数据的到来而更新, 把一次性的分析变成常规监测。

12.1 How to reproduce this report如何复现本报告

The exercise is a self-contained folder inside the course’s Quarto website. Every path in the scripts and in the report is relative to take-home-ex/take-home-ex2/, and the scripts are run from there:


本作业是课程 Quarto 网站中一个自包含的文件夹。脚本与报告中的每一个路径都相对于 take-home-ex/take-home-ex2/,脚本也从这里运行:

# 0. Place the ACLED extract (from eLearn) anywhere under data/raw/
#    e.g. data/raw/acled/ACLED_Data_Myanmar_Jan2021-Sep2025.csv

# 1. Preparation

Rscript scripts/02_acled.R        # ACLED audit, geocoding, panels

# 2. Analysis
Rscript scripts/03_lmsa.R         # global and local Moran's I, Gi*, sensitivity
Rscript scripts/04_ehsa.R         # space-time cube, EHSA, sfdep check, null
Rscript scripts/05_markov.R       # value-added: spatial Markov, FE logit, onsets

# 3. Render, from the site root
quarto render take-home-ex/take-home-ex2/take-home-ex2.qmd
quarto render take-home-ex/take-home-ex2/take-home-ex2-slides.qmd






NoteData that are and are not in the repository



ACLED’s terms of use do not allow the event records to be republished, so the extract itself and the event-level objects built from it (events_sf.rds, conflict_sf.rds) are kept out of the repository. Everything the report reads is aggregated to the township: the panels, the totals, the audit tables and the analysis results in data/derived/, which are committed, so the report renders from a clean clone without the raw data. To re-run the scripts, the ACLED extract has to be obtained from the course or from ACLED directly. The MIMU v9.4 boundary archive is committed, because MIMU replaces its releases and this version may not stay available.








Note仓库中包含与不包含的数据



ACLED 的使用条款不允许重新发布事件记录,因此数据摘录本身,以及由其构建的事件级 对象(events_sf.rds、conflict_sf.rds)都不放入仓库。报告读取的一切都已汇总到 镇区:data/derived/ 中的面板、总量、审计表与分析结果都已提交,因此从一份干净的 克隆出发,无需原始数据即可渲染报告。若要重新运行脚本,需要从课程或直接从 ACLED 获取 数据摘录。MIMU v9.4 边界压缩包已提交,因为 MIMU 会替换其发布版本,该版本未必会一直 可供下载。

text:
12.3 Caching and seeds缓存与随机种子

The permutation tests are the slow part. Each expensive result is computed through cache_rds() in R/utils.R, which stores it in data/cache/ and returns the stored object on later runs. Every script sets set.seed(1234), and functions that draw permutations set their own seed, so deleting data/cache/ and re-running reproduces the same values. A full run from a cold cache takes about 20 minutes, most of it in 04_ehsa.R.


置换检验是耗时的部分。每个耗时结果都通过 R/utils.R 中的 cache_rds() 计算,它把 结果存入 data/cache/,并在之后的运行中直接返回存储的对象。每个脚本都设定了 set.seed(1234),抽取置换的函数也会设定自己的种子,因此删除 data/cache/ 后重新运行, 得到的数值完全相同。从空缓存完整运行一次约需 20 分钟,大部分时间花在 04_ehsa.R 上。

text:
12.5 Source code源代码

The complete source of each script and helper file, inserted from disk at render time so that it cannot drift from what actually ran.


每个脚本与辅助文件的完整源码,在渲染时从磁盘插入,因此不可能与实际运行的版本产生 偏移。


01 boundaries02 ACLED03 LMSA04 EHSA05 value addedR/ehsa.RR/utils.R




Code
# =============================================================================
# 01_boundaries.R -- Myanmar township frame for the analysis
# Take-home Exercise 2 | ISSS626
#
# Reads the MIMU v9.4 township polygons, establishes a working projection by
# measuring distortion rather than assuming one, and records the two
# properties that decide whether a contiguity-based local statistic can be
# computed at all: duplicate identifiers and townships with no neighbours.
# Run from take-home-ex/take-home-ex2/.
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf); library(dplyr); library(spdep)
})

RAW <- "data/raw"; DER <- "data/derived"
dir.create(DER, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# ---- Import -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Read straight from the archive as downloaded from the MIMU GeoNode, so that
# the zip is the only boundary file the repository needs to carry. MIMU replaces
# its boundary releases, and v9.4 may not stay downloadable.
ts <- st_read(paste0("/vsizip/", RAW, "/mmr_polbnda_adm3_250k_mimu_v9_4.zip/",
                     "mmr_polbnda_adm3_250k_mimu_1.shp"), quiet = TRUE)

stopifnot(nrow(ts) == 330L)

# ---- Geometry and identifier integrity --------------------------------------
# A local statistic is indexed by polygon, so a duplicated or missing township
# pcode silently corrupts every join downstream. Both are checked before the
# layer is used for anything.
geom_report <- list(
  n          = nrow(ts),
  invalid    = sum(!st_is_valid(ts)),
  empty      = sum(st_is_empty(ts)),
  dup_pcode  = sum(duplicated(ts$TS_PCODE)),
  na_pcode   = sum(is.na(ts$TS_PCODE) | ts$TS_PCODE == ""),
  multipart  = sum(vapply(st_geometry(ts), function(g) length(g) > 1L, logical(1)))
)

if (geom_report$invalid > 0) ts <- st_make_valid(ts)

# ---- Choosing the working projection ----------------------------------------
# Myanmar spans 92.17-101.17 E, which straddles UTM zones 46N and 47N; neither
# zone covers the country without stretching. Rather than adopt one by
# convention, each candidate is scored on how far its planar area departs from
# the geodesic area of the same polygons, which is the quantity an areal
# analysis actually depends on.
# The reference must be the ELLIPSOIDAL area. With s2 enabled sf measures on a
# sphere, which is itself 0.27% away from the ellipsoid and would mask the very
# distortion being measured; with s2 disabled sf routes geographic coordinates
# to lwgeom's geodesic area, which is computed on WGS 84 itself.
sf_use_s2(FALSE)
area_geod <- as.numeric(st_area(st_transform(ts, 4326)))   # m^2, ellipsoidal

candidates <- c(
  "EPSG:32646" = "EPSG:32646",                 # WGS 84 / UTM 46N
  "EPSG:32647" = "EPSG:32647",                 # WGS 84 / UTM 47N
  # Lambert azimuthal equal area centred on the country's own centroid
  "LAEA_MMR"   = paste0("+proj=laea +lat_0=19.1 +lon_0=96.7 ",
                        "+x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"),
  # Albers equal area with standard parallels set inside Myanmar's latitude span
  "AEA_MMR"    = paste0("+proj=aea +lat_1=12 +lat_2=26 +lat_0=19.1 +lon_0=96.7 ",
                        "+x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs")
)

crs_scores <- lapply(names(candidates), function(nm) {
  a <- as.numeric(st_area(st_transform(ts, candidates[[nm]])))
  data.frame(crs = nm,
             total_err_pct = 100 * abs(sum(a) - sum(area_geod)) / sum(area_geod),
             max_abs_err_pct = max(100 * abs(a - area_geod) / area_geod),
             med_abs_err_pct = median(100 * abs(a - area_geod) / area_geod))
}) |> bind_rows() |> arrange(max_abs_err_pct)

WORK_CRS <- candidates[[crs_scores$crs[1]]]
ts_proj  <- st_transform(ts, WORK_CRS)

# ---- Contiguity ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Queen contiguity is the default neighbour definition for township-level LMSA.
# Myanmar's coast includes island townships, and an island has no queen
# neighbour at all: spdep returns a zero-length neighbour set, which propagates
# as NaN through any row-standardised weight and quietly removes those
# townships from the analysis. They are identified here so the decision about
# them is made explicitly in the report rather than by accident.
nb_queen <- poly2nb(ts_proj, queen = TRUE)
no_nb    <- which(card(nb_queen) == 0L)

islands <- if (length(no_nb)) {
  st_drop_geometry(ts_proj)[no_nb, c("ST", "DT", "TS", "TS_PCODE")]
} else {
  st_drop_geometry(ts_proj)[0, c("ST", "DT", "TS", "TS_PCODE")]
}

nb_report <- list(
  n_links      = sum(card(nb_queen)),
  avg_links    = mean(card(nb_queen)),
  min_links    = min(card(nb_queen)),
  max_links    = max(card(nb_queen)),
  n_no_nb      = length(no_nb),
  n_comp       = n.comp.nb(nb_queen)$nc,
  pct_nonzero  = 100 * sum(card(nb_queen) > 0) / nrow(ts_proj)
)

# ---- The analytical frame and its neighbour structure ------------------------
# Each neighbourless township is resolved on its own merits rather than by one
# blanket rule. The edge-to-edge distance to the nearest township decides it:
# Munaung and Chaungzon lie within a few kilometres of the mainland and are
# linked to their single nearest township, which is how they are reached in
# practice. Cocokyun lies more than 100 km offshore; any neighbour assigned to
# it would be invented, and it carries no ACLED record of any kind (checked in
# 02_acled.R), so it is removed from the analytical frame instead and kept only
# as a cartographic feature.
isl_dist <- lapply(no_nb, function(i) {
  d <- as.numeric(st_distance(ts_proj[i, ], ts_proj)); d[i] <- Inf
  j <- which.min(d)
  data.frame(TS_PCODE = ts_proj$TS_PCODE[i], TS = ts_proj$TS[i],
             nearest = ts_proj$TS[j], nearest_pcode = ts_proj$TS_PCODE[j],
             dist_km = d[j] / 1000)
}) |> bind_rows()

OFFSHORE_KM <- 50
excluded <- isl_dist$TS_PCODE[isl_dist$dist_km > OFFSHORE_KM]
linked   <- isl_dist[isl_dist$dist_km <= OFFSHORE_KM, ]

# The frame is sorted by TS_PCODE. sfdep's emerging_hotspot_analysis() labels
# its output rows in geometry order but computes them in sorted-location
# order, so the two must coincide for the labels to be right (see Section 6
# of the report, where this is demonstrated).
ts_an <- ts_proj |>
  filter(!TS_PCODE %in% excluded) |>
  arrange(TS_PCODE)

nb_an <- poly2nb(ts_an, queen = TRUE)
for (r in seq_len(nrow(linked))) {
  i <- match(linked$TS_PCODE[r], ts_an$TS_PCODE)
  j <- match(linked$nearest_pcode[r], ts_an$TS_PCODE)
  nb_an[[i]] <- sort(unique(c(setdiff(nb_an[[i]], 0L), j)))
  nb_an[[j]] <- sort(unique(c(setdiff(nb_an[[j]], 0L), i)))
}
attr(nb_an, "region.id") <- ts_an$TS_PCODE
stopifnot(all(card(nb_an) > 0), n.comp.nb(nb_an)$nc == 1L,
          is.symmetric.nb(nb_an))

# A second, structurally different neighbour definition is kept for the
# sensitivity analysis. k = 6 nearest neighbours by point-on-surface is close
# to the queen average of about 5.2 links, but every township gets exactly six,
# so large Shan and Kachin townships and small Yangon townships are treated
# alike. It is asymmetric, which row-standardised local statistics tolerate.
pos <- st_coordinates(st_point_on_surface(st_geometry(ts_an)))
nb_knn6 <- knn2nb(knearneigh(pos, k = 6), row.names = ts_an$TS_PCODE)

nb_report$islands_dist <- isl_dist
nb_report$excluded     <- excluded
nb_report$an_n         <- nrow(ts_an)
nb_report$an_avg_links <- mean(card(nb_an))
nb_report$an_max_links <- max(card(nb_an))
nb_report$knn6_sym     <- is.symmetric.nb(nb_knn6)

# ---- Dissolved frames for cartography ---------------------------------------
state  <- ts_proj |> group_by(ST, ST_PCODE) |> summarise(.groups = "drop")
nation <- st_union(ts_proj) |> st_sf(geometry = _)

# ---- Save --------------------------------------------------------------------
saveRDS(list(work_crs = WORK_CRS, crs_scores = crs_scores,
             geom_report = geom_report, nb_report = nb_report,
             islands = islands, area_geod_km2 = sum(area_geod) / 1e6),
        file.path(DER, "bnd_report.rds"))
saveRDS(ts_proj,  file.path(DER, "township.rds"))
saveRDS(ts_an,    file.path(DER, "township_an.rds"))
saveRDS(state,    file.path(DER, "state.rds"))
saveRDS(nation,   file.path(DER, "nation.rds"))
saveRDS(nb_queen, file.path(DER, "nb_queen.rds"))
saveRDS(nb_an,    file.path(DER, "nb_an.rds"))
saveRDS(nb_knn6,  file.path(DER, "nb_knn6.rds"))

cat("\n== CRS candidates (ranked by worst-township area error) ==\n")
print(crs_scores, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
cat("\nselected:", crs_scores$crs[1], "\n")
cat("\n== Geometry ==\n"); str(geom_report)
cat("\n== Queen contiguity ==\n"); str(nb_report)
if (nrow(islands)) { cat("\n== Townships with no queen neighbour ==\n"); print(isl_dist, row.names = FALSE) }
cat("\nexcluded from analysis:", excluded, "\n")
cat("analytical frame:", nrow(ts_an), "townships, mean", round(mean(card(nb_an)), 2), "links\n")
cat("\ngeodesic area of Myanmar:", format(round(sum(area_geod)/1e6), big.mark = ","), "km2\n")






Code
# =============================================================================
# 02_acled.R -- import, audit and geocode the ACLED event records
# Take-home Exercise 2 | ISSS626
#
# Turns the ACLED extract into an audited event-level sf object, the township
# totals the local measures of spatial association are computed on, and the
# township-by-quarter and township-by-month panels the space-time cube is
# built from. Every record that is dropped is counted and the reason is
# recorded, so the report can state what the analysis is run on rather than
# implying it used everything.
# Run from take-home-ex/take-home-ex2/.
# =============================================================================

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(stringr)
  library(lubridate); library(readr)
})

RAW <- "data/raw"; DER <- "data/derived"
dir.create(DER, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

STUDY_START <- as.Date("2021-01-01")
STUDY_END   <- as.Date("2025-09-30")

# ---- Locate the extract ------------------------------------------------------
# The file is distributed through the course rather than fetched from an API,
# so its name is not fixed. Anything in data/raw/ that looks like a tabular
# ACLED export is accepted, and the chosen file is recorded in the audit.
cand <- list.files(RAW, pattern = "\\.(csv|xlsx|xls)$", full.names = TRUE,
                   ignore.case = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
stopifnot("No ACLED extract found in data/raw/" = length(cand) > 0)
src <- cand[which.max(file.size(cand))]

read_any <- function(p) {
  if (grepl("\\.csv$", p, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    readr::read_csv(p, show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = 200000,
                    name_repair = "minimal")
  } else {
    readxl::read_excel(p, guess_max = 200000)
  }
}
raw <- read_any(src)

# ACLED has shipped the same fields under different capitalisation across
# releases; names are normalised once so nothing downstream depends on which
# release produced the file.
names(raw) <- tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", names(raw)))

need <- c("event_date", "event_type", "latitude", "longitude", "fatalities",
          "admin3", "geo_precision", "sub_event_type")
missing_cols <- setdiff(need, names(raw))
stopifnot("ACLED extract is missing required columns" = length(missing_cols) == 0)

n_raw <- nrow(raw)

# ---- Typing ------------------------------------------------------------------
# event_date arrives either as a date or as a string in one of two orders;
# parsing is explicit so that a silent NA never turns into a dropped month.
parse_event_date <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, "Date")) return(x)
  if (inherits(x, "POSIXct")) return(as.Date(x))
  d <- suppressWarnings(lubridate::dmy(x, quiet = TRUE))
  if (sum(is.na(d)) > 0.5 * length(d)) d <- suppressWarnings(lubridate::ymd(x, quiet = TRUE))
  d
}

ev <- raw |>
  mutate(
    event_date = parse_event_date(event_date),
    latitude   = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(latitude)),
    longitude  = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(longitude)),
    fatalities = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(fatalities)),
    across(any_of(c("geo_precision", "time_precision", "year")),
           ~ suppressWarnings(as.integer(.x)))
  )

# ---- Audit: the reasons a record cannot be used ------------------------------
# Counted before any filtering so the proportions in the report refer to the
# extract as delivered.
audit <- list(
  source_file   = basename(src),
  n_raw         = n_raw,
  n_cols        = ncol(raw),
  n_dup_id      = if ("event_id_cnty" %in% names(ev)) sum(duplicated(ev$event_id_cnty)) else NA_integer_,
  n_bad_date    = sum(is.na(ev$event_date)),
  n_out_window  = sum(!is.na(ev$event_date) &
                      (ev$event_date < STUDY_START | ev$event_date > STUDY_END)),
  n_no_coord    = sum(is.na(ev$latitude) | is.na(ev$longitude)),
  n_zero_coord  = sum(!is.na(ev$latitude) & !is.na(ev$longitude) &
                      ev$latitude == 0 & ev$longitude == 0),
  n_na_fatal    = sum(is.na(ev$fatalities)),
  geo_precision = table(ev$geo_precision, useNA = "ifany"),
  time_precision= if ("time_precision" %in% names(ev)) table(ev$time_precision, useNA = "ifany") else NULL,
  event_type    = sort(table(ev$event_type), decreasing = TRUE),
  disorder_type = if ("disorder_type" %in% names(ev)) sort(table(ev$disorder_type), decreasing = TRUE) else NULL,
  country       = if ("country" %in% names(ev)) sort(table(ev$country), decreasing = TRUE) else NULL,
  date_range    = range(ev$event_date, na.rm = TRUE),
  # ACLED's timestamp is the last time a record was modified. Its maximum dates
  # the extract, which matters because ACLED revises and back-fills records.
  extracted     = if ("timestamp" %in% names(ev))
                    as.Date(as.POSIXct(max(as.numeric(ev$timestamp), na.rm = TRUE),
                                       origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")) else NA
)

# ---- Filtering ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Duplicates are removed on ACLED's own event identifier rather than on the
# whole row: two genuinely distinct events can share a date, a location and an
# event type, and dropping one of them would understate intensity.
ev2 <- ev |>
  { \(d) if ("event_id_cnty" %in% names(d)) distinct(d, event_id_cnty, .keep_all = TRUE) else d }() |>
  filter(!is.na(event_date), event_date >= STUDY_START, event_date <= STUDY_END) |>
  filter(!is.na(latitude), !is.na(longitude), !(latitude == 0 & longitude == 0))

# The Myanmar extract also carries a handful of maritime records coded to the
# "Indian Ocean" pseudo-country. They have no township and are removed here.
if ("country" %in% names(ev2)) {
  audit$n_not_myanmar <- sum(ev2$country != "Myanmar")
  audit$not_myanmar   <- ev2 |> filter(country != "Myanmar") |>
    count(country, event_type, sub_event_type)
  ev2 <- filter(ev2, country == "Myanmar")
}

audit$n_after_filter <- nrow(ev2)

# ---- Geocoding to townships --------------------------------------------------
# The join is spatial rather than by name. ACLED carries its own admin3 string,
# but it is maintained against ACLED's gazetteer and not against MIMU v9.4, so
# matching on text would silently lose every township whose romanisation
# differs. The name field is kept and compared afterwards as a check on the
# spatial join rather than as the join key. The join is made against all 330
# MIMU townships, so that an event falling in the township later excluded from
# the analytical frame would be seen rather than silently lost.
ts    <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "township.rds"))
ts_an <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "township_an.rds"))
WORK_CRS <- st_crs(ts)

ev_sf <- st_as_sf(ev2, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326,
                  remove = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(WORK_CRS)

sf_use_s2(FALSE)
idx <- st_within(ev_sf, ts, sparse = TRUE)
hit <- lengths(idx) > 0L

# Events that fall just outside a polygon -- coastal rounding, or a coordinate
# on a boundary line -- are recovered by nearest township, but only within a
# tolerance. Beyond it the record is dropped rather than attached to a
# township it may not belong to.
NEAR_TOL <- 5000  # metres

ev_sf$ts_idx <- NA_integer_
ev_sf$ts_idx[hit] <- vapply(idx[hit], function(i) i[1], integer(1))

if (any(!hit)) {
  out <- which(!hit)
  nn  <- st_nearest_feature(ev_sf[out, ], ts)
  dd  <- as.numeric(st_distance(ev_sf[out, ], ts[nn, ], by_element = TRUE))
  ok  <- dd <= NEAR_TOL
  ev_sf$ts_idx[out[ok]] <- nn[ok]
  audit$n_outside_poly  <- length(out)
  audit$n_snapped       <- sum(ok)
  audit$n_dropped_far   <- sum(!ok)
  audit$max_snap_dist_m <- if (any(ok)) max(dd[ok]) else 0
} else {
  audit$n_outside_poly <- 0L; audit$n_snapped <- 0L
  audit$n_dropped_far <- 0L; audit$max_snap_dist_m <- 0
}

ev_sf <- ev_sf |>
  filter(!is.na(ts_idx)) |>
  mutate(TS_PCODE = ts$TS_PCODE[ts_idx],
         TS       = ts$TS[ts_idx],
         DT       = ts$DT[ts_idx],
         ST       = ts$ST[ts_idx],
         ym       = floor_date(event_date, "month"),
         yq       = floor_date(event_date, "quarter"))

audit$n_geocoded    <- nrow(ev_sf)
audit$n_in_excluded <- sum(!ev_sf$TS_PCODE %in% ts_an$TS_PCODE)

# Agreement between the spatial join and ACLED's own admin3 label. This is a
# check, not a correction: disagreement is expected where the two gazetteers
# romanise differently, and the figure tells the reader how much.
norm   <- function(x) tolower(gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(x)))
has_a3 <- !is.na(ev_sf$admin3)
audit$admin3_agreement_pct <-
  100 * mean(norm(ev_sf$admin3[has_a3]) == norm(ev_sf$TS[has_a3]))
audit$admin3_disagree <- st_drop_geometry(ev_sf)[has_a3, ] |>
  filter(norm(admin3) != norm(TS)) |>
  count(acled_admin3 = admin3, mimu_township = TS, sort = TRUE)

# ---- What counts as an armed-conflict event -----------------------------------
# ACLED's six event types are not all armed conflict. Protests and riots are
# demonstrations; strategic developments record non-violent activity such as
# arrests, troop movements and territorial transfers. The three event types
# ACLED itself groups as political violence carry the analysis, and each is kept
# as its own variable because they are produced by different actors and should
# not be assumed to share a geography.
CONFLICT_TYPES <- c("Battles", "Explosions/Remote violence",
                    "Violence against civilians")

ev_sf <- ev_sf |>
  mutate(
    is_conflict = event_type %in% CONFLICT_TYPES,
    # Two location problems make a record unusable at township level even
    # though the spatial join succeeds. Records whose admin3 is missing were
    # placed by ACLED at a city reference point ("Mandalay - Unspecified",
    # "Yangon - Unspecified", "Nay Pyi Taw"): the city is known, the township
    # is not, and the join puts every one of them into whichever township holds
    # the reference point. Records at geo_precision 3 are known only to a
    # district or state and are coded at its capital. Both would manufacture a
    # concentration that the underlying events do not have.
    loc_city_only   = is.na(admin3),
    loc_region_only = geo_precision == 3,
    usable_loc      = !loc_city_only & !loc_region_only
  )

audit$city_only <- st_drop_geometry(ev_sf) |>
  filter(loc_city_only) |>
  count(location, mimu_township = TS, conflict = is_conflict, sort = TRUE)

audit$loc_flow <- st_drop_geometry(ev_sf) |>
  filter(is_conflict) |>
  summarise(
    conflict_geocoded = n(),
    city_only         = sum(loc_city_only),
    region_only       = sum(loc_region_only & !loc_city_only),
    analysed          = sum(usable_loc),
    fatal_geocoded    = sum(fatalities),
    fatal_analysed    = sum(fatalities[usable_loc])
  )

audit$exclusion_by_type <- st_drop_geometry(ev_sf) |>
  filter(is_conflict) |>
  group_by(event_type) |>
  summarise(geocoded = n(), city_only = sum(loc_city_only),
            region_only = sum(loc_region_only & !loc_city_only),
            analysed = sum(usable_loc),
            prec1 = sum(usable_loc & geo_precision == 1),
            prec2 = sum(usable_loc & geo_precision == 2),
            .groups = "drop")

# "Excessive force against protesters" is lethal state violence, but ACLED
# files it under the Protests event type. It is counted here so that the report
# can say how much of the 2021 crackdown falls outside the conflict variables.
audit$excessive_force <- st_drop_geometry(ev_sf) |>
  filter(sub_event_type == "Excessive force against protesters") |>
  summarise(n = n(), fatalities = sum(fatalities),
            first = min(event_date), last = max(event_date))

conf <- ev_sf |> filter(is_conflict, usable_loc)

audit$time_precision_conf <- table(conf$time_precision)

# ---- The space-time panels ---------------------------------------------------
# A space-time cube has to be complete: every township present in every period,
# including the townships and periods with no recorded event. Those zeroes are
# data -- a township with no reported violence in a quarter is exactly the
# observation a cold spot is built from -- so each panel is completed against
# the full grid rather than left as the sparse set of rows ACLED supplies.
# Quarters are the primary time unit and months are kept for the sensitivity
# analysis; both run over the 329 townships of the analytical frame.
make_panel <- function(d, time_col, periods) {
  d |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    group_by(TS_PCODE, period = .data[[time_col]]) |>
    summarise(
      conflict   = n(),
      battles    = sum(event_type == "Battles"),
      erv        = sum(event_type == "Explosions/Remote violence"),
      vac        = sum(event_type == "Violence against civilians"),
      fatalities = sum(fatalities),
      airstrike  = sum(sub_event_type == "Air/drone strike"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    complete(TS_PCODE = ts_an$TS_PCODE, period = periods,
             fill = list(conflict = 0L, battles = 0L, erv = 0L, vac = 0L,
                         fatalities = 0, airstrike = 0L)) |>
    arrange(period, TS_PCODE)
}

months   <- seq(floor_date(STUDY_START, "month"),   floor_date(STUDY_END, "month"),   by = "month")
quarters <- seq(floor_date(STUDY_START, "quarter"), floor_date(STUDY_END, "quarter"), by = "quarter")

panel_m <- make_panel(conf, "ym", months)
panel_q <- make_panel(conf, "yq", quarters)

stopifnot(nrow(panel_m) == nrow(ts_an) * length(months),
          nrow(panel_q) == nrow(ts_an) * length(quarters),
          sum(panel_q$conflict) == nrow(conf),
          sum(panel_m$conflict) == nrow(conf))

# Whole-period township totals: the input to the local measures of spatial
# association.
tot <- conf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(TS_PCODE) |>
  summarise(conflict   = n(),
            battles    = sum(event_type == "Battles"),
            erv        = sum(event_type == "Explosions/Remote violence"),
            vac        = sum(event_type == "Violence against civilians"),
            fatalities = sum(fatalities),
            airstrike  = sum(sub_event_type == "Air/drone strike"),
            .groups = "drop")

ts_tot <- ts_an |>
  left_join(tot, by = "TS_PCODE") |>
  mutate(across(c(conflict, battles, erv, vac, fatalities, airstrike),
                ~ tidyr::replace_na(.x, 0)),
         area_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 1e6)

# Calendar years are kept as well, for the year-by-year LISA. 2025 covers nine
# months only, so any comparison of levels across years is made per month.
panel_y <- conf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(year = year(event_date)) |>
  count(TS_PCODE, year, name = "conflict") |>
  complete(TS_PCODE = ts_an$TS_PCODE, year = 2021:2025,
           fill = list(conflict = 0L)) |>
  mutate(months = ifelse(year == 2025, 9L, 12L))

# ---- Aggregates for the report --------------------------------------------------
# ACLED's terms of use do not allow the event records themselves to be
# republished, so everything the report draws from is aggregated here: no
# derived object read by the report holds an individual event.
# Location precision by township: the share of each township's events that
# ACLED could only place "near" a town rather than at a named village.
ts_prec <- conf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  group_by(TS_PCODE) |>
  summarise(n = n(), share_prec2 = mean(geo_precision == 2), .groups = "drop")
ts_tot <- ts_tot |> left_join(ts_prec |> select(TS_PCODE, share_prec2), by = "TS_PCODE")

# Who initiates each kind of event, by year. ACLED's inter1 code classifies the
# first actor; it is the closest the data come to attributing an event.
audit$actor_year <- conf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(year = year(event_date)) |>
  count(year, event_type, actor_type = inter1)

audit$sub_event_year <- conf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(year = year(event_date)) |>
  count(year, event_type, sub_event_type)

# State-level totals by quarter and event type, for the trend figures.
audit$state_quarter <- conf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(ST, yq, event_type)

audit$n_months   <- length(months)
audit$n_quarters <- length(quarters)
audit$pct_zero_q <- 100 * mean(panel_q$conflict == 0)
audit$pct_zero_m <- 100 * mean(panel_m$conflict == 0)
audit$n_ts_zero  <- sum(ts_tot$conflict == 0)

# ---- Save --------------------------------------------------------------------
saveRDS(ev_sf,   file.path(DER, "events_sf.rds"))
saveRDS(conf,    file.path(DER, "conflict_sf.rds"))
saveRDS(panel_q, file.path(DER, "panel_q.rds"))
saveRDS(panel_m, file.path(DER, "panel_m.rds"))
saveRDS(panel_y, file.path(DER, "panel_y.rds"))
saveRDS(ts_tot,  file.path(DER, "ts_tot.rds"))
saveRDS(audit,   file.path(DER, "acled_audit.rds"))
unlink(file.path(DER, "panel.rds"))

cat("\n== Source ==\n"); cat(audit$source_file, " extracted", format(audit$extracted), "\n")
cat("\n== Record flow ==\n")
cat(sprintf("%-28s %8d\n", "raw rows",             audit$n_raw))
cat(sprintf("%-28s %8d\n", "not Myanmar",          audit$n_not_myanmar))
cat(sprintf("%-28s %8d\n", "after date/coord/dup", audit$n_after_filter))
cat(sprintf("%-28s %8d\n", "geocoded to township", audit$n_geocoded))
cat(sprintf("%-28s %8d\n", "outside any polygon",  audit$n_outside_poly))
cat(sprintf("%-28s %8d\n", "snapped within 5 km",  audit$n_snapped))
cat(sprintf("%-28s %8d\n", "in excluded township", audit$n_in_excluded))
cat("\n== Conflict events, location usability ==\n"); print(audit$loc_flow)
print(audit$exclusion_by_type)
cat("\n== admin3 agreement ==", round(audit$admin3_agreement_pct, 3), "%\n")
print(audit$admin3_disagree)
cat("\n== Excessive force against protesters ==\n"); print(audit$excessive_force)
cat("\n== Panels ==\n")
cat(sprintf("quarterly: %d x %d, %.1f%% zero | monthly: %d x %d, %.1f%% zero | townships with no conflict event: %d\n",
            nrow(ts_an), audit$n_quarters, audit$pct_zero_q,
            nrow(ts_an), audit$n_months, audit$pct_zero_m, audit$n_ts_zero))
print(summary(st_drop_geometry(ts_tot)[, c("conflict", "battles", "erv", "vac", "fatalities")]))
